<div class="container">
    <div class="guide-header">
        <div class="breadcrumb"><a href="/">Home</a> / <a href="/guides/">Guides</a> / AWS Security</div>
        <h1>AWS Security Best Practices</h1>
        <span class="new-badge"><i class="fas fa-cloud"></i> Cloud</span>
        <p style="color: var(--text-muted); font-size: 1.1rem; margin-top: 1rem;">Secure your AWS environment from
            day one with comprehensive hardening guidelines.</p>
        <div class="meta" style="margin-top: 1rem;">
            <div class="meta-item"><i class="fas fa-book-open"></i> 25 min read</div>
            <div class="meta-item"><i class="fas fa-crosshairs"></i> Intermediate</div>
            <div class="meta-item"><i class="far fa-calendar-alt"></i> Jan 17, 2026</div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <article class="content">
        <img src="/images/guides/aws-security-best-practices.png" alt="AWS Security Best Practices Guide"
            class="featured-image" loading="lazy">

        <p>AWS powers millions of organizations worldwide, making it a prime target for attackers. Misconfigurations
            are the #1 cause of cloud breaches - from exposed S3 buckets to overly permissive IAM roles. This guide
            covers the essential security controls every AWS environment needs.</p>

        <div class="info-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-lightbulb"></i> The AWS Shared Responsibility Model</strong>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;"><strong>AWS is responsible for:</strong> Physical
                security, hypervisor, network infrastructure<br><strong>You are responsible for:</strong> IAM, data
                encryption, network configuration, application security, OS patching</p>
        </div>

        <div class="toc">
            <h3><i class="fas fa-list-ul"></i> Table of Contents</h3>
            <ul>
                <li><a href="#account">1. Account Security Fundamentals</a></li>
                <li><a href="#iam">2. IAM Best Practices</a></li>
                <li><a href="#s3">3. S3 Bucket Security</a></li>
                <li><a href="#vpc">4. VPC and Network Security</a></li>
                <li><a href="#logging">5. Logging and Monitoring</a></li>
                <li><a href="#encryption">6. Data Encryption</a></li>
                <li><a href="#detection">7. Threat Detection</a></li>
                <li><a href="#compliance">8. Compliance and Auditing</a></li>
            </ul>
        </div>

        <h2 id="account">1. Account Security Fundamentals</h2>

        <h3>Root Account Protection</h3>
        <div class="warning-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"></i> Critical: Secure Your Root Account</strong>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;">The root account has unlimited access to everything.
                Compromise of root means total account takeover.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="success-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> Root Account Checklist</strong>
            <ul style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li>Enable MFA (hardware key preferred, TOTP minimum)</li>
                <li>Never create access keys for root</li>
                <li>Use a dedicated email with strong security</li>
                <li>Only use root for tasks that require it</li>
                <li>Set up alternate contacts for billing/security</li>
            </ul>
        </div>

        <h3>AWS Organizations</h3>
        <p>For multi-account environments, use AWS Organizations:</p>
        <ul>
            <li><strong>Service Control Policies (SCPs)</strong> - Restrict what services accounts can use</li>
            <li><strong>Consolidated billing</strong> - Single payer, multiple accounts</li>
            <li><strong>Account isolation</strong> - Separate prod/dev/security accounts</li>
        </ul>

        <h2 id="iam">2. IAM Best Practices</h2>

        <h3>The Principle of Least Privilege</h3>
        <p>Grant only the minimum permissions required for a task:</p>

        <div class="aws-box">
            <h5><i class="fas fa-user-shield"></i> Good vs Bad IAM Policy</h5>
            <pre><code><span class="aws-comment">// BAD - Too permissive</span>

{ “Effect”: “Allow”, “Action”: “s3:”, “Resource”: “” }

// GOOD - Specific actions and resources { “Effect”: “Allow”, “Action”: [ “s3:GetObject”, “s3:ListBucket” ], “Resource”: [ “arn:aws:s3:::my-app-bucket”, “arn:aws:s3:::my-app-bucket/*” ] } 

        <h3>IAM Roles vs Access Keys</h3>
        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Use Case</th>
                    <th>Solution</th>
                    <th>Why</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                <tr>
                    <td>EC2 accessing S3</td>
                    <td>IAM Role (Instance Profile)</td>
                    <td>No keys to manage or rotate</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Lambda functions</td>
                    <td>IAM Role (Execution Role)</td>
                    <td>Automatic, secure</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Cross-account access</td>
                    <td>IAM Role with AssumeRole</td>
                    <td>No shared credentials</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>CI/CD pipelines</td>
                    <td>OIDC Federation</td>
                    <td>No long-lived keys</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Local development</td>
                    <td>SSO / Identity Center</td>
                    <td>Temporary credentials</td>
                </tr>
            </tbody>
        </table>

        <h3>IAM Access Analyzer</h3>
        <p>Enable IAM Access Analyzer to find:</p>
        <ul>
            <li>Resources shared with external accounts</li>
            <li>Unused permissions (for policy trimming)</li>
            <li>Public or cross-account access paths</li>
        </ul>

        <pre><code><span class="aws-comment"># AWS CLI - Create analyzer</span>

aws accessanalyzer create-analyzer
–analyzer-name my-analyzer
–type ACCOUNT

        <h2 id="s3">3. S3 Bucket Security</h2>

        <div class="warning-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"></i> S3 Misconfigurations = Data Breaches</strong>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;">Public S3 buckets have caused countless data leaks.
                Always assume your buckets contain sensitive data.</p>
        </div>

        <h3>S3 Block Public Access</h3>
        <p>Enable at the <strong>account level</strong> to prevent any bucket from becoming public:</p>

        <pre><code><span class="aws-comment"># Enable Block Public Access for entire account</span>

aws s3control put-public-access-block
–account-id 123456789012
–public-access-block-configuration
“BlockPublicAcls=true,
IgnorePublicAcls=true,
BlockPublicPolicy=true,
RestrictPublicBuckets=true”

        <h3>S3 Security Checklist</h3>
        <div class="success-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> Every S3 Bucket Should Have:</strong>
            <ul style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li>Block Public Access enabled</li>
                <li>Default encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS)</li>
                <li>Versioning enabled</li>
                <li>Access logging enabled</li>
                <li>Lifecycle policies for old versions</li>
                <li>Object Lock for compliance data (if required)</li>
            </ul>
        </div>

        <h3>Secure Bucket Policy Example</h3>
        <pre><code>{
<span class="aws-keyword">"Version"</span>: <span class="aws-value">"2012-10-17"</span>,
<span class="aws-keyword">"Statement"</span>: [
    {
        <span class="aws-keyword">"Sid"</span>: <span class="aws-value">"DenyInsecureTransport"</span>,
        <span class="aws-keyword">"Effect"</span>: <span class="aws-value">"Deny"</span>,
        <span class="aws-keyword">"Principal"</span>: <span class="aws-value">"*"</span>,
        <span class="aws-keyword">"Action"</span>: <span class="aws-value">"s3:*"</span>,
        <span class="aws-keyword">"Resource"</span>: [
            <span class="aws-value">"arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket"</span>,
            <span class="aws-value">"arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*"</span>
        ],
        <span class="aws-keyword">"Condition"</span>: {
            <span class="aws-keyword">"Bool"</span>: {<span class="aws-keyword">"aws:SecureTransport"</span>: <span class="aws-value">"false"</span>}
        }
    }
]

}

        <h2 id="vpc">4. VPC and Network Security</h2>

        <h3>Security Groups Best Practices</h3>
        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Rule</th>
                    <th>Bad Practice</th>
                    <th>Good Practice</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                <tr>
                    <td>Inbound SSH</td>
                    <td>0.0.0.0/0:22</td>
                    <td>VPN/Bastion IP only</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Inbound RDP</td>
                    <td>0.0.0.0/0:3389</td>
                    <td>Never public; use SSM</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Database</td>
                    <td>All IPs:3306</td>
                    <td>App security group only</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>Outbound</td>
                    <td>All traffic allowed</td>
                    <td>Restrict to needed destinations</td>
                </tr>
            </tbody>
        </table>

        <h3>VPC Flow Logs</h3>
        <p>Enable VPC Flow Logs for network visibility:</p>
        <pre><code>aws ec2 create-flow-logs \
--resource-type VPC \
--resource-ids vpc-12345678 \
--traffic-type ALL \
--log-destination-type cloud-watch-logs \
--log-group-name /aws/vpc/flowlogs</code></pre>

        <h3>Use VPC Endpoints</h3>
        <p>Keep traffic private with VPC Endpoints:</p>
        <ul>
            <li><strong>Gateway Endpoints</strong> - S3, DynamoDB (free)</li>
            <li><strong>Interface Endpoints</strong> - Other AWS services (paid)</li>
        </ul>

        <h2 id="logging">5. Logging and Monitoring</h2>

        <h3>CloudTrail - The Foundation</h3>
        <p>CloudTrail logs all API activity. Enable it in <strong>all regions</strong>:</p>

        <div class="success-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> CloudTrail Configuration</strong>
            <ul style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li>Create organization trail (if using Organizations)</li>
                <li>Enable in all regions</li>
                <li>Log to S3 bucket with versioning + encryption</li>
                <li>Enable log file integrity validation</li>
                <li>Send to CloudWatch Logs for alerting</li>
                <li>Protect trail from tampering with SCPs</li>
            </ul>
        </div>

        <h3>CloudWatch Alarms</h3>
        <p>Set up alarms for critical security events:</p>
        <ul>
            <li>Root account usage</li>
            <li>IAM policy changes</li>
            <li>Security group changes</li>
            <li>CloudTrail disabled</li>
            <li>Console login without MFA</li>
        </ul>

        <h2 id="encryption">6. Data Encryption</h2>

        <h3>Encryption at Rest</h3>
        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Service</th>
                    <th>Default Encryption</th>
                    <th>Recommended</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                <tr>
                    <td>S3</td>
                    <td>Optional</td>
                    <td>SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>EBS</td>
                    <td>Optional (can enforce)</td>
                    <td>Enable account-level default</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>RDS</td>
                    <td>Optional</td>
                    <td>Enable at creation</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td>DynamoDB</td>
                    <td>SSE enabled by default</td>
                    <td>Use KMS CMK for more control</td>
                </tr>
            </tbody>
        </table>

        <h3>KMS Key Policies</h3>
        <p>Use AWS KMS for key management. Control access with key policies:</p>
        <pre><code>{
<span class="aws-keyword">"Sid"</span>: <span class="aws-value">"Allow use of the key"</span>,
<span class="aws-keyword">"Effect"</span>: <span class="aws-value">"Allow"</span>,
<span class="aws-keyword">"Principal"</span>: {
    <span class="aws-keyword">"AWS"</span>: <span class="aws-value">"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/MyAppRole"</span>
},
<span class="aws-keyword">"Action"</span>: [
    <span class="aws-value">"kms:Encrypt"</span>,
    <span class="aws-value">"kms:Decrypt"</span>,
    <span class="aws-value">"kms:GenerateDataKey"</span>
],
<span class="aws-keyword">"Resource"</span>: <span class="aws-value">"*"</span>

}

        <h2 id="detection">7. Threat Detection</h2>

        <h3>Amazon GuardDuty</h3>
        <p>GuardDuty is AWS's threat detection service. Enable it in all accounts and regions:</p>
        <ul>
            <li>Analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs</li>
            <li>Detects crypto mining, data exfiltration, backdoors</li>
            <li>Machine learning identifies anomalies</li>
            <li>Integrates with Security Hub</li>
        </ul>

        <h3>Security Hub</h3>
        <p>Centralize security findings from multiple services:</p>
        <ul>
            <li>GuardDuty findings</li>
            <li>Inspector findings</li>
            <li>IAM Access Analyzer</li>
            <li>Config Rules compliance</li>
            <li>Third-party tools</li>
        </ul>

        <h2 id="compliance">8. Compliance and Auditing</h2>

        <h3>AWS Config Rules</h3>
        <p>Continuously monitor configuration compliance:</p>

        <pre><code><span class="aws-comment"># Essential Config Rules</span>

  • s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited

  • s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only

  • iam-root-access-key-check

  • iam-user-mfa-enabled

  • ec2-security-group-attached-to-eni

  • vpc-flow-logs-enabled

  • cloudtrail-enabled
